sources.source: Optional local CSV assigning acquisition sessions independently of plates. Use an exact filename column, including each merged NPY or selected reference TIFF/NPY suffix, and the selected session column. Every current sample and reference file must have one unique nonblank assignment. Blank keeps one session per plate. Default blank.

Exact column name in the sessions CSV that identifies an acquisition session. All fields in a session share reference gains and must use compatible measurement intensity planes and working units. Default session.

Optional local folder of bead or reference-well images, replacing reference images inside the measured folder. Filenames keep the plate, well and field identity; selected reference wells still apply. NPY files use the merged channel and mask layout. TIFF files contain only intensity channels with explicit spatial and channel axes. No time or ambiguous page-axis interpretation is guessed. Default blank.

Exact acquisition session identifier to use as the gain reference. Blank uses the first session by name, or the sole session on the explicitly selected reference plate. If both plate and session are selected they must agree. A plate assigned to multiple sessions requires this choice. Default blank.

Calibrate intensities before measuring, using beads or reference wells acquired in each imaging session. By default each plate is a session. An optional sessions CSV assigns fields independently of plates; an external bead folder can supply the reference images. Gains match the selected reference session or plate; blank choices keep the first-by-name default. The existing camera-offset gain method is unchanged. Gains and reference content identities are recorded in measurements.db:intensity_rescale. Default False.
sources.old_source: Calibrate intensities across imaging sessions before measuring: each plate is one session, the beads or reference wells imaged on every plate are measured, and every plate's intensity channels are scaled so its reference wells match the selected reference plate's; a blank reference plate setting uses the first plate by name. This corrects exposure, lamp and detector drift between days at the image level, unlike batch correction of tables. The gains are recorded in measurements.db:intensity_rescale. Default False.

sources.source: Wells holding the same calibration sample in each acquisition session, such as ['A01'] or ['A01', 'P24']. References come from the selected external bead folder, or otherwise the measured merged folder. Every measured session must have a usable reference field. In-source reference wells are measured like any other well. Default None.
sources.old_source: The wells holding the calibration sample, imaged on every plate with the same sample: fluorescent beads or a reference stain, such as ['A01'] or ['A01', 'P24']. Every plate must have at least one field in them, or the run stops. They are measured and calibrated like any other well. Default None.

sources.source: Exact reference plate identifier from merged filenames, such as plate2. Without a sessions CSV, blank keeps the first plate by name. With explicit sessions, this plate must belong to one session, or pair it with an exact reference session on that plate. The selected plate must be present in the measured run. Default blank.
sources.old_source: Reference plate identifier from the merged filenames, such as plate2. Leave blank to use the first plate by name. The selected plate must be present in this run. Default blank.

sources.source: How each reference field intensity is summarised after subtracting intensity_calibration_offset. foreground is the median above Otsu for sparse beads on a dark background; median uses all pixels for a uniformly stained reference well. Each acquisition session uses the median over its reference fields. Default foreground.
sources.old_source: How each reference field's intensity is summarised, after subtracting intensity_calibration_offset. foreground: the median of the pixels above an Otsu threshold, for sparse beads on a dark background. median: the median of all pixels, for a uniformly stained reference well. Each plate uses the median over its reference fields. Default foreground.
